quizName: DMV Practice Test #3 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is just part of riding a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause permanent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind noise from long-term riding can permanently damage your hearing. Wear ear protection when you ride. It will protect your hearing while still letting you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a crash, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use proper lane positions.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible, use turn signals, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changing conditions.

questions.question: Blind spots on motorcycles:

options.text: Should be checked regularly by riders.
Don't exist if the motorcycle has a rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be checked regularly by riders.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks part of your regular riding routine.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They warn you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: A passenger should sit:
questions.correctAnswerText: Behind the operator.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit behind the operator and hold onto the operator's waist or midsection. They can also hold onto handgrips if the motorcycle has them. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: A DOT-approved helmet:

options.text: Lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
Can become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lets you see far enough to the sides for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see everything you need to ride safely.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine since over-the-counter medications are weak.
May affect your riding and should be done carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding and should be done carefully.
questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter and prescription medications have side effects that can impair your ability to ride safely. Always talk to your doctor about how a medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: When scanning the area around your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Look for escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
See if you can travel faster than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look for escape routes near intersections, shopping areas, and schools.
questions.explanation: While looking for hazards, focus on finding escape routes in intersections, shopping areas, schools, and construction zones.

questions.question: When wearing a helmet during a crash, a rider is:

options.text: Less likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
Just as likely to survive as someone without a helmet.
More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: More likely to survive than someone without a helmet.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries than riders wearing helmets, regardless of speed.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should:

options.text: Follow each other as closely as possible.
Not worry about distances between members.

questions.correctAnswerText: All maintain safe following distances.
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, use a staggered formation. This keeps the group close while maintaining safe following distances between riders.

questions.question: Unlike other beverages, alcohol:
questions.correctAnswerText: Enters the bloodstream right away.
questions.explanation: Alcohol does not need to be digested like other foods and drinks. It passes directly through the stomach and small intestine walls into the bloodstream and reaches the brain quickly.

questions.question: When a motorcyclist needs to stop quickly, they should:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes at the same time. Look ahead at the road to help you avoid needing to stop suddenly.

questions.question: When stopping your motorcycle while carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
Merge into smaller traffic gaps than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Start slowing down earlier than normal.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight makes the motorcycle slower to respond. It takes longer to speed up, slow down, and turn. Start slowing down earlier when you stop and look for larger gaps when crossing or merging into traffic.

questions.question: Improper braking:

options.text: Is not a concern because motorcycles have two brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Causes many motorcycle crashes.
questions.explanation: Improper braking causes many motorcycle crashes. Using correct braking technique is important for safe riding.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is coming.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: When nearing a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will yield to you.
Move to a different lane position so other drivers can see you better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane position so other drivers can see you better.
questions.explanation: When approaching a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: As your motorcycle goes faster, you will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift up to higher gears.
questions.explanation: You must shift into higher gears as your motorcycle speeds up.

questions.question: When wearing a jacket for protection, the jacket should:

options.text: Be loose and flap in the wind while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly.
questions.explanation: Riding clothes should protect you while keeping you comfortable. Jackets and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: To reduce the chance of a crash, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds in front of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, look ahead at least 10 to 15 seconds in front of your motorcycle. Looking ahead gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
Stop only to yield to other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must stop completely, let all crossing traffic and pedestrians pass, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Focus only on what is in front of you.
Focus only on what is behind you.
Be aware of what is in front of and behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be aware of what is in front of and behind you.
questions.explanation: Watch the road ahead and check your mirrors regularly to see what is behind you. Both are important for safe riding.

questions.question: Is lane sharing allowed?

options.text: Yes, it is encouraged in heavy traffic.
Yes, if vehicles are going slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is usually prohibited.
questions.explanation: Both cars and motorcycles need a full lane to operate safely. Lane sharing is usually not allowed.

questions.question: What clothing should you wear when riding?
questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear bright colors so other drivers can see you. Reflective materials also help you stay visible.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding during the day?

options.text: Bright clothing to help others see you.
Any color because it is easy to see in daylight.
Dark clothing to stand out against the sunlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright clothing to help others see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Always wear bright colors to stay visible, even during the day.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: It marks the right edge of the traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road shows where the right edge of the traffic lane is.
